title: dquickts
brief: dquickts is a QuickJS fork adding durable execution: suspend a running JS program mid-loop, serialize the whole heap to bytes, and resume it in another process. It also runs TypeScript natively (no transpile step), ships a durable REPL whose session survives restarts, and includes Rust bindings. - Warning: brand-new repo (created 19 Oct 2026, ~357 stars); license field shows NOASSERTION.
details: dquickts is a fork of Fabrice Bellard's QuickJS embeddable JavaScript engine that adds durable execution: you can pause a running program even in the middle of a for loop, serialize the whole heap to bytes, and resume it later in a different process. It runs TypeScript natively with no transpile step, ships a durable REPL (qjs --drepl FILE) whose session survives restarts, and includes Rust bindings. Use cases: hibernating idle scripts to disk, durable workflows that span hours, time-slicing computation across machines, and warm starts from snapshots.
